lesson_title: The Debt That Shrinks From the Wrong End: Annuities
hook_text: Eighteen months of faithful bakkie payments — nearly R83 000 paid. The bank's settlement figure? R121 138 STILL owed. Here's the arithmetic.
clip_script: You borrow 180 000 rand for a bakkie. Four years, 0,875 percent a month, instalment 4 608 rand. Eighteen months in, you have paid faithfully — nearly 83 000 rand. You ask the bank for a settlement figure. They reply: 121 138 rand, please. Two THIRDS of the loan still standing. A trick? No — arithmetic. Picture your debt as a water tank. Every month, interest pours in: a fixed percentage of whatever currently sits in the tank. Your instalment bails out a fixed bucket. Month one, the tank is brim-full — interest pours in 1 575 rand, so your 4 608 bucket removes only 3 034 of real debt. The fuller the tank, the harder interest pushes back. Only near the end does each bucket land almost whole. Debt drains slowly first, fast last — from the wrong end. But the tank hands you the defence: an extra rand paid EARLY strikes the water when it is deepest, cancelling years of the interest that rand would have bred. Early overpayments punch far above late ones. That is annuity mathematics — and it is consumer self-defence.
visual_style: A glass water tank labelled with the loan balance, an interest pipe pouring in at the top and a bucket bailing at fixed size, a split bar in each instalment showing interest versus real repayment shifting over forty-eight months.
mood: Eye-opening, protective, a friend explaining the fine print.
pacing: Calm setup, a jolt at the settlement figure, methodical through the tank months, empowering close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any loan the way the bank does.
